Συναυλία

ΑΠΟΣΤΟΛΗΣ ΜΠΑΡΜΠΑΓΙΑΝΝΗΣ Τσολιάς εν δε Τσόλια Μπαντ «ΟΠΕΚΕΜΠΛΕ»

Τετάρτη 11 Φεβρουαρίου στις 00:00 | ΣΤΑΥΡΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΝΟΤΟΥ

The tsoliades — those skirted soldiers who guard the Parliament — march in your imagination. Then you realize tonight's tsolias is dancing, and the kilt is spinning with intent. At Stavros tou Notou, Apostolis Barbagiannis brings OPEKEMBLE.

The name sounds like nonsense until you hear it: a collision of Greek folk tradition with whatever else the evening demands. Barbagiannis has built a reputation for performances that refuse the museum approach to tradition. The foustanella skirt appears, but the music that accompanies it has absorbed decades of contamination — jazz, rock, the electric possibilities that tradition's guardians pretend don't exist.

Stavros tou Notou occupies its own position in the Athens live music landscape. The venue programs Greek music that knows its history but refuses to be imprisoned by it. The room is intimate enough for the energy to circulate, the crowd close enough to participate. When Barbagiannis launches into material, the traditional dance steps mix with whatever else people feel like moving.

The crowd self-selects wonderfully. You won't find tourists seeking "authentic Greek music" — this is too strange for that. You will find Greeks who understand that tradition lives by changing, musicians from adjacent scenes curious about the collision, the adventurous who follow Stavros tou Notou's programming wherever it leads. By the second set, inhibitions dissolve.

If you want rebetiko in its preserved form, if tradition should remain untouched, OPEKEMBLE operates as provocation. Barbagiannis takes what's inherited and asks what it can become. But if you've been waiting for Greek music that's genuinely alive, that treats tradition as raw material rather than museum display — tonight, the tsolias proves what the dance can still do.
